info.title: resend-conversation-service API
info.description: Receives signed Resend webhooks and provides bearer-authenticated topic-centered conversations plus synchronous and queued direct email. Conversation API v2 is the only conversation contract; conversation API v1 was retired in 0.5.0 and its paths are no longer routed. The service persists outbound intent before contacting Resend, preserves RFC reply relationships for conversations, and stores untrusted email content without retrieving attachments. The separate AsyncAPI contract for conversation lifecycle events is available from the deployed service at `/asyncapi.json`.

tags.name: Conversations
tags.description: Create, assign, and hydrate email conversations

tags.name: Messages
tags.description: Send messages in an existing conversation

tags.name: Direct email
tags.description: Synchronously send or enqueue email without a conversation or Reply-To header

tags.name: Outbox
tags.description: Asynchronous message enqueue and bounded batch delivery

get.description: Checks configuration for every webhook, conversation, and outbox capability plus PostgreSQL connectivity without returning sensitive details.

503.description: Required configuration or PostgreSQL is unavailable.

post.description: Verifies the Svix signature against the exact raw request body, classifies the event, and stores its normalized fields. For email.received, the service retrieves the text, HTML, and headers from Resend and updates the conversation projection; attachments are not fetched. Eligible RFC Message-ID ancestry remains authoritative. When RFC ancestry does not resolve a conversation, a recognized conversation token in to or received_for is used only when the sender matches that conversation's participant. Reconciliation of out-of-order rows preserves one-way V2 promotion and historical routing-token/base aliases when conversations merge. All three Svix headers are required and must describe the submitted body. A delivery using an svix-id already stored for the same event family is acknowledged with the same 200 response after projection succeeds. Resend may retry non-200 responses. Swagger UI cannot generate valid Svix signatures; interactive requests require header values generated for the exact raw request body.

requestBody.description: A supported Resend event serialized as JSON. The serialized bytes must be the same bytes used to generate svix-signature.

200.description: The event was stored, or an event with the same svix-id was already stored for its event family.

400.description: One or more required Svix headers are missing, or the signed event type does not belong to a recognized Resend event family.

401.description: The Svix signature could not be verified against the exact raw request body.

500.description: The server is missing required configuration, could not retrieve inbound content, or could not persist the event and projection. Resend can retry the delivery.

post.summary: Send a direct email without a conversation
post.description: Persists a direct outbound email intent and synchronously sends it through Resend. The normalized from.address must exactly match a FROM allowlist entry; recipients are not allowlisted. No conversation, parent, routing token, Reply-To header, or RFC threading headers are created. Without a Reply-To header, mail clients normally direct replies to the From address.

201.description: Resend accepted the newly persisted email.

202.description: An idempotent replay found intent that is still pending.

502.description: The persisted send failed or its provider outcome is indeterminate.

post.summary: Enqueue a direct email without a conversation
post.description: Atomically persists a pending direct email and shared outbox entry without calling Resend. Validation, multiple-recipient support, tags, exact FROM authorization, and Reply-To rejection match the synchronous direct-email operation. Later allowlist removal does not cancel already-persisted intent. Replaying the same key and normalized queued request returns 202 while pending, 200 after acceptance, or 502 after a failed or indeterminate drain outcome.

200.description: A matching queued request was already accepted by Resend.

202.description: The direct email is durably queued and remains pending.

502.description: The queued email was later marked failed or indeterminate.

post.description: Delivers one bounded, ordered batch from the shared transactional outbox. It uses only OUTBOX_DRAIN_API_KEY and may deliver direct and conversation messages in one fixed ordered batch. This is the only drain route; invoke it at least once per minute when using queued sends. The service can also drive this same drain internally on a cron schedule instead of an external caller; that scheduler is disabled by default and is configured with OUTBOX_DRAIN_SCHEDULE_ENABLED and OUTBOX_DRAIN_SCHEDULE. A retryable provider failure preserves the fixed batch and provider idempotency key for a later invocation inside the safety window. Final failed or indeterminate outcomes are terminal and are not retried.

200.description: The bounded shared drain invocation completed, including persisted retry scheduling when applicable.

post.summary: Start a topic conversation with explicit identities
post.description: Creates the single conversation for an external topic and sends its opening email. message.from and message.replyTo are required structured identities. Optional message.to recipients override the outbound recipient list but do not change the single conversation participant; when omitted, the email is sent to participant. Optional message.tags are forwarded to Resend. From and Reply-To normalized addresses must have exact allowlist rows for the FROM and REPLY_TO roles respectively. The Reply-To address must be an untagged base address; the service persists it for the conversation and sends from base-local+c_<32 lowercase hex routing token>@domain. Identity or fixed-base rejection uses one generic 400 response. A failed V1 topic conversation may be reopened and promoted to V2 when all prior messages are failed and its persisted Reply-To base is absent or equals the requested base. Promotion occurs when the V2 intent is successfully persisted, before the provider call, so a subsequent 502 does not undo it.

200.description: An earlier completed request with this idempotency key was returned.

201.description: Conversation created, or a failed topic conversation reopened and promoted to V2, and the opening email accepted by Resend.

202.description: An earlier request with this idempotency key is still pending.

400.description: The request is malformed, failed validation, or requested an identity or Reply-To base that is not allowed. Authorization policy rejection is deliberately generic.

value.error: The requested email identity is not allowed. Contact the administrator.

409.description: The idempotency key conflicts or the topic already has a conversation with at least one message that is not failed.

502.description: Resend did not accept the email or the send result is indeterminate. If this request reopened a V1 conversation, its V2 promotion was already committed with the persisted intent.

get.description: V2 mirror of the unassigned conversation list. Reads are not version-filtered.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Opaque cursor returned by the previous unassigned-conversation page.

get.description: Returns conversation counts for every state plus a paginated list of conversations in the selected states, ordered by oldest state change first so state=awaiting_us reads as a reply queue. Items carry conversation metadata only; read messages from the conversation endpoint. Reads are not version-filtered.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Restrict the list to these states. Repeat the parameter or pass a comma-separated list; values are matched case-insensitively. Omit to list every state. The counts object always covers all four states regardless of this filter.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Opaque cursor returned by the previous state-summary page.

200.description: Conversation counts per state and the selected page.

post.summary: Queue a topic conversation with explicit identities
post.description: Atomically creates the V2 conversation, pending opening message, and outbox entry. Identity allowlist and fixed Reply-To base rules match the synchronous V2 operation. Allowlist authorization is frozen into the queued message; later allowlist removal does not cancel an already-authorized outbox intent. Replaying the same idempotency key and normalized request returns 202 while the stored message remains pending, 200 after acceptance, or 502 after a failed or indeterminate outcome.

200.description: An earlier completed outbox request with this idempotency key was returned.

202.description: The persisted V2 opening message is pending outbox delivery, including an idempotent replay while that stored message remains pending.

400.description: The request is malformed, failed validation, or requested an identity or Reply-To base that is not allowed. Authorization policy rejection is deliberately generic.

502.description: An earlier outbox request completed as failed or indeterminate.

get.summary: Get a conversation by service ID
get.description: Reads any conversation visible to the service, including V1 conversations; reading does not promote it to V2.

200.description: Conversation and a chronological page of messages.

patch.summary: Assign an unassigned conversation through V2
patch.description: Assigns a topic exactly once and records the conversation as V2. The conversation must be unassigned and its API version must be null or already V2; a V1 conversation cannot be assigned through this operation.

post.description: Operator override for the conversation state, most commonly marking a conversation concluded when it needs no follow-up. Every state is settable and every transition is permitted, including reopening a terminated conversation. Setting the state a conversation already holds succeeds and leaves the state value unchanged, but currently resets stateChangedAt. No email is sent or enqueued, so no Idempotency-Key is required.

200.description: The conversation with its updated state.

post.summary: Continue a conversation with explicit identities
post.description: Sends a reply using required from and replyTo identities. Optional to recipients override the outbound recipient list but do not change the single conversation participant; when omitted, the reply is sent to participant. Optional tags are forwarded to Resend. Exact role-specific allowlist rows are checked before conversation lookup. The requested Reply-To base must equal the conversation's persisted base once set. Persisting the V2 reply intent atomically promotes a V1 conversation to V2. Promotion does not require provider acceptance and remains committed if the subsequent synchronous provider call returns 502. An explicit reply parent must belong to the conversation; otherwise the latest accepted or received message is used, and References is built from that parent's ancestry.

200.description: An earlier completed request with this idempotency key was returned.

201.description: Reply accepted by Resend; a V1 conversation is promoted to V2 as part of persistence.

202.description: An earlier request with this idempotency key is still pending.

400.description: The request is malformed, failed validation, or requested an identity or Reply-To base that is not allowed. Authorization policy rejection is deliberately generic.

example.error: The requested email identity is not allowed. Contact the administrator.

502.description: Resend did not accept the email or the send result is indeterminate. When replying to a V1 conversation, V2 promotion was already committed with the persisted intent.

503.description: The selected parent RFC Message-ID could not be retrieved.

post.summary: Queue a conversation reply with explicit identities
post.description: Resolves and freezes the reply parent, RFC ancestry, approved identities, and generated Reply-To address, then atomically creates a pending message and outbox entry. A V1 conversation is promoted to V2 when the queued intent is persisted. Later allowlist removal does not cancel that queued intent. Replaying the same idempotency key and normalized request returns 202 while the stored message remains pending, 200 after acceptance, or 502 after a failed or indeterminate outcome.

200.description: An earlier completed outbox request with this idempotency key was returned.

202.description: The persisted V2 reply is pending outbox delivery, including an idempotent replay while that stored message remains pending; a V1 conversation is promoted to V2 as part of persistence.

400.description: The request is malformed, failed validation, or requested an identity or Reply-To base that is not allowed. Authorization policy rejection is deliberately generic.

502.description: An earlier outbox request completed as failed or indeterminate.

503.description: The selected parent RFC Message-ID could not be retrieved.

get.summary: Get a conversation by external topic
get.description: Reads any conversation for the topic, including V1 conversations; reading does not promote it to V2.

200.description: Conversation and a chronological page of messages.

emailV2Auth.description: Current V2 credential supplied from EMAIL_v2_API_KEY or the EMAIL_V2_API_KEY fallback. EMAIL_v2_API_KEY takes precedence when both are nonempty. It authorizes conversation V2 operations and direct email; it is not interchangeable with the outbox-drain credential.

outboxDrainAuth.description: Dedicated credential for the private scheduled outbox drain caller.

svixId.name: svix-id
svixId.description: Unique Svix message identifier used for signature verification and idempotency.

svixTimestamp.name: svix-timestamp
svixTimestamp.description: Svix delivery timestamp included in signature verification.

svixSignature.name: svix-signature
svixSignature.description: Svix signature generated for the exact raw request body.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Caller-generated key unique to one logical send request. Idempotency compares normalized validated fields; unknown body properties are ignored and do not produce a conflict. Keys are globally unique across direct email, API versions, and synchronous and outbox delivery modes.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Public contract for read pagination. Send an integer from 1 through 100; clients must not rely on the current implementation's lenient parsing of invalid values.

Before.name: before
Before.description: Return messages older than this internal message ID. The ID must belong to the requested conversation.

externalId.description: Public contract maximum is 255 characters. The topic lookup route currently only rejects empty values; clients must keep this field within the documented contract. Path usage requires URL encoding.

title.description: Trimmed, header-safe text: at least one non-whitespace character and no ASCII control characters.

email.description: Runtime validation also limits the address to 320 characters.

name.description: Header-safe text: no ASCII control characters. Blank values are normalized to null.

address.description: Trimmed and normalized to lowercase. Authorization requirements depend on the request field.

name.description: Optional header-safe display name. Blank or null values normalize to null.

EmailRecipientList.description: One recipient identity or an array of 1-50 recipient identities. A singular identity is accepted for compatibility.

EmailTags.description: Optional Resend tags forwarded with the provider send request. Blank names or values are rejected.

allOf.description: The address must be an untagged base mailbox with no plus tag and enough local-part space for +c_<32 lowercase hex>. It is normalized to lowercase and must exactly match a REPLY_TO allowlist row. The service appends the conversation routing token; callers must never submit the generated tagged address.

text.description: Plain text body. Must be a nonempty string when present.

html.description: HTML body. Must be a nonempty string when present.

from.description: Required sender identity. The normalized address must exactly match a database allowlist row with role FROM.

to.description: Optional outbound recipients. When omitted, conversation sends target the single conversation participant. Recipients are not allowlisted and do not become conversation participants.

subject.description: Defaults to the topic title after trimming and stripping leading Re:/Fw:/Fwd: prefixes. Header-safe text: no ASCII control characters. Blank values are omitted.

CreateConversationV2Request.description: V2 does not support the V1 message.replyToName property; use message.replyTo.name.

replyToMessageId.description: Internal message ID in this conversation. Defaults to the latest accepted or received message.

CreateMessageV2Request.description: V2 does not support the V1 replyToName property; use replyTo.name.

from.description: Sender identity. The normalized address must exactly match a database allowlist row with role FROM.

to.description: Recipient identity or nonempty recipient identity array. Recipients are not checked against the identity allowlist.

subject.description: Required nonblank header-safe subject. Leading and trailing whitespace is removed.

DirectEmailV2Request.description: Direct email intentionally does not support Reply-To or threading fields.

before.description: Opaque base64url cursor for the next unassigned-conversation page.

limit.description: Maximum number of unbatched messages to assign when creating a new batch.

stateDetail.description: Human-readable provider or runtime detail. Not stable for machine parsing.

deliveryState.description: Outbound-only delivery lifecycle projected from Resend delivery webhooks. Inbound messages return null. unknown means no delivery lifecycle webhook has been projected yet.

deliveryStateDetail.description: Human-readable delivery detail from Resend webhook payloads. Not stable for machine parsing.

deliveredAt.description: Timestamp from the first projected email.delivered webhook for outbound messages, or null when no delivery confirmation has been projected.

replyTo.description: For outbound messages, the stable conversation routing address generated by appending +c_<32 lowercase hex token> to the persisted base. V2 obtains and fixes it from the first authorized caller-supplied replyTo.address. For inbound messages, this is the sender-provided Reply-To address when present.

replyToName.description: For outbound messages, the optional per-message display name used with the service-generated Reply-To address. Inbound messages currently return null.

ConversationState.description: Whose turn the conversation is on. Inbound mail sets awaiting_us; persisting outbound reply intent sets awaiting_participant; a bounced, complained, or suppressed outbound delivery sets terminated. Automatic transitions never move a terminated conversation, and inbound mail reopens a concluded one.

ConversationStateCounts.description: Conversation totals per state across the whole service, independent of any state filter.

ConversationStateSummaryItem.description: Conversation metadata only. Messages are deliberately not included; read them from the conversation endpoint.

count.description: Total conversations across the selected states, independent of the returned page.

replyToAddress.description: Stable generated Reply-To routing address. Its base is fixed on first outbound intent and the same per-conversation +c_<32 lowercase hex token> is preserved.

stateChangedAt.description: For automatic mail-flow transitions, when the conversation last entered its current state. Automatic transitions only move it when the state value changes, so for awaiting_us it records how long the reply has been owed. A successful manual state write currently resets it, including a repeated state value.

awaitingReply.description: Derived from state; true exactly when state is awaiting_us.

resendEmailId.description: Provider identifier after acceptance; null while pending or when no acceptance was confirmed.

from.description: Sender address as supplied by Resend.

message_id.description: RFC Message-ID supplied for inbound email.received events.

reason.description: Provider-supplied failure reason, such as reached_daily_quota.

BadRequest.description: The request is malformed or failed validation.

Unauthorized.description: The bearer credential is missing or invalid. Bearer-protected endpoints include `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`.

WWW-Authenticate.description: Bearer authentication challenge returned by bearer-protected endpoints.

NotFound.description: The requested conversation or message does not exist.

Conflict.description: The topic, assignment, or idempotency key conflicts with existing state.

PayloadTooLarge.description: The uncompressed raw request body exceeds the 2100 KB transport limit.

UnsupportedContentEncoding.description: Compressed request bodies are rejected before route processing. Send uncompressed JSON without Content-Encoding compression.

example.error: Compressed request bodies are not supported

ServerError.description: The service is misconfigured or could not persist the operation.
